1→# Hummingbird is Down — Can You Fix It?
     2→
     3→## The Scenario
     4→
     5→You're a new engineer on the Hummingbird team. It's your first week. The senior engineer is on
     6→vacation. Support tickets are coming in. You have Claude Code, a terminal, and `curl`.
     7→
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Your Environment
    11→
    12→| What              | How to access                                                             |
    13→|------------       |---                                                                        |
    14→| Source code       | Which you cloned in your current directory                                |
    15→| CloudWatch logs   | `aws logs tail /ecs/hummingbird/production/api --follow`                  |
    16→| Claude Code       | `export ANTHROPIC_MODEL='us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1'` then `claude`  |
    17→
    18→> **Start here — confirm the API is up:**
    19→> ```bash
    20→> curl http://<alb-dns>/health
    21→> ```
    22→> You should see `{"status":"ok","service":"hummingbird"}`.
    23→
    24→---
    25→
    26→## Understand the System First
    27→
    28→Before touching any bug, open Claude Code and ask:
    29→
    30→```
    31→Give me a high-level walkthrough of this codebase.
    32→What is the full lifecycle of an uploaded image — from POST /upload to GET /download?
    33→Which file and function handles each step?
    34→```
    35→
    36→---
    37→
    38→## The Tickets
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### Ticket #1 — "Server started on the wrong port" *(Easy)*
    43→
    44→> *"A teammate forgot `APP_PORT` in their `.env` file. The server started — no crash,
    45→> no error — but it wasn't on port 9000. The log said `listening on port undefined`."*
    46→
    47→**Investigate with Claude Code:**
    48→```
    49→In server.js, how is the port determined?
    50→What happens in Node.js when you call app.listen(undefined)?
    51→Is there any fallback or guard?
    52→```
    53→
    54→**Fix accepted when:** `server.js` uses `process.env.APP_PORT || 9000`.
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### Ticket #2 — "Width is missing from metadata" *(Easy)*
    59→
    60→> *"I upload with `?width=800`. I call `GET /v1/media/:id` straight after.
    61→> The response has `size`, `name`, `status` — but no `width` anywhere."*
    62→
    63→**Reproduce it:**
    64→```bash
    65→curl -X POST "http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/upload?width=800" -F "file=@sample.jpg"
    66→curl http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>
    67→```
    68→
    69→**Investigate with Claude Code:**
    70→```
    71→In clients/dynamodb.js, what fields does createMedia save to DynamoDB?
    72→Now look at what getMedia returns. Are all the same fields present?
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Fix accepted when:** `getMedia` return object includes `width: Number(Item.width.N)`.
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→### Ticket #3 — "Your redirect URL is broken" *(Intermediate)*
    80→
    81→> *"I try to download while the image is still processing. I get a `202` — fine.
    82→> But the `Location` header says:*
    83→> ```
    84→> Location: hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com/v1/media/abc/status
    85→> ```
    86→> *No `http://`. My client can't follow it."*
    87→
    88→**Reproduce it:**
    89→```bash
    90→curl -X POST "http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/upload?width=500" -F "file=@sample.jpg"
    91→curl -i http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>/download
    92→```
    93→
    94→Look at the `Location` header in the output.
    95→
    96→**Investigate with Claude Code:**
    97→```
    98→In the downloadController in controllers/media.js, show me how the Location header is built.
    99→What does req.hostname return vs req.get('host') in Express?
   100→What does a valid Location header look like for a 3xx response?
   101→```
   102→
   103→**Fix accepted when:** Location value starts with `http://` and includes the host and port.
   104→
   105→---
   106→
   107→### Ticket #4 — "Download never redirects even when COMPLETE" *(Intermediate)*
   108→
   109→> *"`GET /status` says `COMPLETE`. `GET /download` still returns `202`. Every time. Forever."*
   110→
   111→**Reproduce it:**
   112→```bash
   113→curl -X POST "http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/upload?width=500" -F "file=@sample.jpg"
   114→curl -X PUT "http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>/resize?width=500"
   115→curl http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>/status
   116→curl -i http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>/download
   117→```
   118→
   119→Check CloudWatch — the `downloadController` logs the `currentStatus` on every 202:
   120→```bash
   121→aws logs tail /ecs/hummingbird/production/api --follow
   122→```
   123→
   124→**Investigate with Claude Code:**
   125→```
   126→In the downloadController in controllers/media.js, what condition decides
   127→whether to return a 202 vs a 302?
   128→Is that comparison correct given that COMPLETE status should trigger the redirect?
   129→```
   130→
   131→**Fix accepted when:** The condition checks `media.status !== MEDIA_STATUS.COMPLETE`.
   132→
   133→---
   134→
   135→## Bonus — "Status never changes. No errors. Nothing." *(Advanced)*
   136→
   137→> *"`PUT /resize` responds `{ status: 'COMPLETE' }`. `GET /status` says `PENDING`.
   138→> Resize again — still `PENDING`. Zero errors in the logs. The resize appears to work every time."*
   139→
   140→Tail logs while triggering a resize:
   141→```bash
   142→aws logs tail /ecs/hummingbird/production/api --follow &
   143→curl -X PUT "http://<alb-dns>/v1/media/<mediaId>/resize?width=500"

> *"A teammate forgot `APP_PORT` in their `.env` file. The server started — no crash,

In server.js, how is the port determined?
What happens in Node.js when you call app.listen(undefined)?
Is there any fallback or guard?
```

**Fix accepted when:** `server.js` uses `process.env.APP_PORT || 9000`.

### Ticket #2 — "Width is missing from metadata" *(Easy)*

> *"I upload with `?width=800`. I call `GET /v1/media/:id` straight after.

```

**Investigate with Claude Code:**

> *"I try to download while the image is still processing. I get a `202` — fine.
> But the `Location` header says:*

What does req.hostname return vs req.get('host') in Express?

```

Here's a high-level walkthrough of the **Hummingbird** codebase:

## What It Is

A Node.js/Express REST API for uploading images, storing metadata, processing them (resize), and serving downloads. It runs on AWS (ECS Fargate behind an ALB) and uses S3, DynamoDB, SNS, and SQS.

## Project Structure

```
humming-bird-midterm/
├── server.js                  # Express app entry point (health check, mounts routes)
├── routes/media.js            # Route definitions for /v1/media/*
├── controllers/media.js       # Request handlers (upload, status, download, get, resize, delete)
├── actions/uploadMedia.js     # Streaming upload logic using formidable + S3
├── clients/
│   ├── s3.js                  # S3 operations (upload, download URL, copy, delete)
│   ├── dynamodb.js            # DynamoDB CRUD for media metadata
│   └── sns.js                 # Publishes events to SNS (resize, delete)
├── worker/processor.js        # Background SQS consumer that processes resize/delete events
├── core/
│   ├── constants.js           # Shared constants (statuses, event types, file limits, widths)
│   ├── responses.js           # HTTP response helpers (200, 202, 400, 404, 500)
│   └── utils.js               # Utility (bytes→MB conversion)
├── middlewares/
│   ├── validateWidth.js       # Validates width param is within 100–1024
│   └── setMediaWidth.js       # Extracts width from query/body, defaults to 500
├── observability/             # OpenTelemetry instrumentation
├── terraform/                 # Infrastructure-as-code (ECS, ALB, ECR, S3, DynamoDB, IAM, VPC)
├── Dockerfile                 # Container image definition
└── logger.js                  # Winston logger setup
```

## Full Lifecycle of an Uploaded Image

### 1. Upload — `POST /v1/media/upload?width=500`

- **Middlewares** (`validateWidth` → `setMediaWidth`): validate and parse the `width` query param, attach it to `req.hummingbirdOptions`.
- **Controller** (`controllers/media.js:uploadController`): calls `uploadMedia(req)`.
- **Action** (`actions/uploadMedia.js`): uses **formidable** to parse the multipart form. Overrides `file.open` to create a `Transform` stream that pipes directly to **S3** via `uploadMediaToStorage()` — so the file streams to S3 without buffering the whole thing in memory. Stores under `uploads/<mediaId>/<filename>`.
- Back in the controller: writes metadata to **DynamoDB** via `createMedia()` (mediaId, size, name, mimetype, width, status=`PENDING`).
- Publishes a `media.v1.resize` event to **SNS** via `publishResizeMediaEvent()`.
- Returns **202 Accepted** with `{ mediaId }`.

### 2. Background Processing — Worker (`worker/processor.js`)

- Long-polls an **SQS** queue subscribed to the SNS topic.
- On a `media.v1.resize` message: sets status to `PROCESSING`, copies the file from `uploads/` to `resized/` in S3, then sets status to `COMPLETE`.
- On a `media.v1.delete` message: deletes both S3 objects and the DynamoDB record.

### 3. Check Status — `GET /v1/media/:id/status`

- `statusController` reads metadata from DynamoDB via `getMedia()`, returns `{ status }` (one of `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `COMPLETE`, `ERROR`).

### 4. Download — `GET /v1/media/:id/download`

- `downloadController` checks the media's status in DynamoDB.
- If not complete: returns **202** with `Retry-After` and `Location` headers pointing to the status endpoint.
- If complete: generates a **presigned S3 URL** and returns a **302 redirect**.

### 5. Manual Resize — `PUT /v1/media/:id/resize`

- `resizeController` does the resize synchronously (copy in S3 + status updates in DynamoDB) so it works even without the background worker, then also publishes the SNS event.

### 6. Delete — `DELETE /v1/media/:id`

- `deleteController` publishes a `media.v1.delete` SNS event. The worker handles actual cleanup.

## Key AWS Services

| Service | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| **S3** | Stores original (`uploads/`) and processed (`resized/`) images |
| **DynamoDB** | Media metadata (PK: `MEDIA#<id>`, SK: `METADATA`) |
| **SNS** | Event bus for resize and delete events |
| **SQS** | Queue consumed by the background worker |
| **ECS Fargate** | Runs the API and worker containers |
| **ALB** | Load balancer in front of the API |

This is also set up as a **debugging exercise** (see `ASSIGNMENT.md`) with several intentional bugs planted for students to find and fix.

## Step 1: Request Hits the Route

**`routes/media.js:15`** — The POST is matched and passes through two middlewares before the controller:

```
router.post('/upload', validateWidth, setMediaWidth, uploadController);
```

1. **`middlewares/validateWidth.js:13`** — Reads `width` from the query string (or body). If provided, checks it's an integer between 100–1024. Rejects with 400 if invalid. Passes through if absent (width is optional).

2. **`middlewares/setMediaWidth.js:12`** — Parses the width and attaches it to `req.hummingbirdOptions.width`, defaulting to `500` if not provided.

## Step 2: Streaming Upload to S3

**`controllers/media.js:27-78`** (`uploadController`) calls **`actions/uploadMedia.js:25`** (`uploadMedia`).

Inside `uploadMedia`:
- A `mediaId` is generated via `crypto.randomUUID()` (line 29)
- **formidable** parses the multipart form data with constraints: max 1 file, images only, 100 MB limit
- On `fileBegin` (line 71), `file.open` is overridden to create a `Transform` stream that pipes directly into **`clients/s3.js:22`** (`uploadMediaToStorage`)
- The file is streamed (not buffered) to S3 at key: **`uploads/<mediaId>/<originalFilename>`**
- On completion, resolves with `{ mediaId, file }` (the formidable file JSON)

## Step 3: Save Metadata to DynamoDB

Back in `uploadController` (line 33):

**`clients/dynamodb.js:23`** (`createMedia`) writes a `PutItem` to DynamoDB:

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `PK` | `MEDIA#<mediaId>` |
| `SK` | `METADATA` |
| `size` | file size in bytes |
| `name` | original filename |
| `mimetype` | e.g. `image/jpeg` |
| `status` | **`PENDING`** |
| `width` | requested width |

## Step 4: Publish Resize Event to SNS

Still in `uploadController` (line 35):

**`clients/sns.js:56`** (`publishResizeMediaEvent`) publishes a JSON message to the SNS topic:

```json
{
  "type": "media.v1.resize-media",
  "payload": { "mediaId": "<uuid>", "width": 500 }
}
```

The controller then returns **202 Accepted** with `{ mediaId }` to the caller.

## Step 5: Background Worker Picks Up the Event

SNS fans out to an SQS queue. **`worker/processor.js:95`** (`pollForever`) long-polls SQS with `ReceiveMessageCommand` (20-second wait, up to 10 messages at a time).

When a message arrives:
1. **`parseBody`** (line 16) unwraps the SNS envelope to get the inner message
2. **`handleMessage`** (line 75) routes on `type` — for `media.v1.resize`, calls `handleResize`
3. **`handleResize`** (line 30):
   - Fetches metadata via `getMedia(mediaId)` to get the filename

message.content: In server.js, how is the port determined?
What happens if process.env.APP_PORT is undefined?

content.text:
Exactly what I described above — Node's `http.Server.listen()` receives `undefined` as the port argument. In that case:

1. **No crash, no error** — Node treats it the same as calling `app.listen(0)`, which tells the OS to assign a **random ephemeral port** (e.g. 49152, 54321, etc.)
2. **The log is misleading** — it prints `Example app listening on port undefined` (line 38), suggesting everything started fine
3. **The server is unreachable** — anything expecting port 9000 (the ALB, health checks, `curl`) can't connect because the server is on some random port

It's a silent failure — the process is running and healthy from its own perspective, but nothing can reach it.

message.content: Is there any fallback or guard?

content.text:
No. There is no fallback, no default value, and no validation. Line 35 is simply:

```js
const port = process.env.APP_PORT;
```

If the env var is missing, `port` is `undefined` and the server silently starts on a random port. There's no code that:

- Provides a default (e.g. `|| 9000`)
- Throws an error if the value is missing
- Logs a warning about a missing configuration

To fix this, add a fallback on `server.js:35`:

```js
const port = process.env.APP_PORT || 9000;
```

message.content: In the downloadController in controllers/media.js, show me how the Location header is built.

content.text:
From `controllers/media.js:111`:

```js
res.set('Location', `${req.hostname}/v1/media/${mediaId}/status`);
```

There are two problems here:

1. **No protocol** — `req.hostname` returns just the hostname (e.g. `hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com`) without `http://`. So the Location header becomes:
   ```
   Location: hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com/v1/media/abc/status
   ```
   Clients can't follow that — it's not a valid URL.

2. **No port** — `req.hostname` strips the port. If the server runs on a non-standard port, it's lost.

The fix is to use `req.get('host')` (which includes the port) and prepend the protocol:

```js
res.set('Location', `http://${req.get('host')}/v1/media/${mediaId}/status`);
```

This is **Ticket #3**. Want me to apply it?

message.content: What does req.hostname return vs req.get('host') in Express?

content.text:
In Express:

- **`req.hostname`** — Returns only the hostname portion, stripped of the port. For example: `hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com`

- **`req.get('host')`** — Returns the value of the `Host` HTTP header, which includes the port if present. For example: `hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com:9000`

Neither includes the protocol (`http://` or `https://`). The current code uses `req.hostname` with no protocol prefix, so the Location header is invalid on two counts — missing scheme and missing port.

message.content: What does a valid Location header look like for a 3xx response?

content.text:
A valid `Location` header must be a full absolute URI per the HTTP spec:

```
Location: http://hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com:9000/v1/media/abc/status
```

It needs:
- **Protocol** — `http://` or `https://`
- **Host + port** — `hostname:port` (port can be omitted for 80/443)
- **Path** — the resource path

The current code produces:

```
Location: hummingbird-alb-xxx.elb.amazonaws.com/v1/media/abc/status
```

Which is missing the `http://` prefix and the port — clients will fail to follow it.

message.content:
Compare the DynamoDB key used in createMedia, getMedia, and setMediaStatus
in clients/dynamodb.js. Are all three targeting the exact same item?

content.text:
No. There's a casing mismatch in `setMediaStatus`:

| Function | PK | SK | Line |
|----------|----|----|------|
| `createMedia` | `MEDIA#<mediaId>` | `METADATA` | `dynamodb.js:29` |
| `getMedia` | `MEDIA#<mediaId>` | `METADATA` | `dynamodb.js:62` |
| **`setMediaStatus`** | `MEDIA#<mediaId>` | **`metadata`** | `dynamodb.js:154` |

`setMediaStatus` uses lowercase `'metadata'` while the other two use uppercase `'METADATA'`. DynamoDB keys are case-sensitive, so `setMediaStatus` targets a **different item** that doesn't exist.

The result: DynamoDB's `UpdateItem` with no `ConditionExpression` silently **creates a new item** with key `SK: metadata` instead of updating the existing `SK: METADATA` record. That's why status never changes — the update goes to a phantom row.

This is the **Bonus Ticket**. The fix is to change line 154 from `'metadata'` to `'METADATA'`. Want me to apply it?

message.content:
What does DynamoDB do when UpdateItem is called on a key that doesn't exist
and there is no ConditionExpression?

content.text:
DynamoDB **silently creates a new item**. Without a `ConditionExpression`, `UpdateItem` is an **upsert** — if no item matches the key, it creates one with just the key attributes and the updated fields.

So when `setMediaStatus` runs with `SK: 'metadata'`:

1. No item exists with key `{ PK: "MEDIA#<id>", SK: "metadata" }`
2. DynamoDB creates a **new item**: `{ PK: "MEDIA#<id>", SK: "metadata", status: "COMPLETE" }`
3. The **original item** with `SK: "METADATA"` is untouched — still `PENDING`
4. No error is thrown

That's why `PUT /resize` returns `{ status: "COMPLETE" }` (the controller trusts its own writes) but `GET /status` still reads `PENDING` (it queries with `SK: "METADATA"`, which was never updated).

whether to return a 202 vs a 302?

content.text:
From `controllers/media.js:108`:

```js
if (media.status !== MEDIA_STATUS.PROCESSING) {
```

This is **backwards**. It returns 202 (not ready) when the status is anything other than `PROCESSING`. That means when status is `COMPLETE`, it still returns 202.

The logic should be: return 202 when the media is **not yet complete**, i.e.:

if (media.status !== MEDIA_STATUS.COMPLETE) {
```

message.content: Is that comparison correct given that COMPLETE status should trigger the redirect?

content.text:
No, it's inverted. The current logic:

- `status !== PROCESSING` → return **202** (not ready)
- `status === PROCESSING` → return **302** (redirect to download)

That means `COMPLETE` hits the `!== PROCESSING` branch and returns 202 forever. The only status that would trigger a redirect is `PROCESSING`, which is the exact opposite of what you want.

The correct check should be:

```js
if (media.status !== MEDIA_STATUS.COMPLETE) {
```

So that:
- `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `ERROR` → **202** (not ready, retry later)
- `COMPLETE` → **302** (redirect to presigned S3 URL)
